reason: Every load-bearing claim reproduces. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 on ?v=light&state=loading&motion=settled: document.querySelector('.sk-wrap').innerText returns the whole reading -- 31, +5 ON THE FOUR BEFORE, 'jobs finished, Harbour House weddings - this week still running', 6, 12, 12 SO FAR, the five week ticks, OPEN NOW 9, 'jobs not finished', 3 / 2 / 1 / 0 with all four sentences, and OLDEST 41 DAYS. A real Ctrl+A does not merely select it, it PAINTS it: the after-selection screenshot shows white glyphs on the selection blue in every one of those positions, at full value, because Blink's selection foreground overrides the color:transparent that is the only thing hiding them. lately.html:486-494 is the whole hiding mechanism and it is colour and visibility only; there is no user-select rule and no ::selection rule anywhere in the file. The JS neutralising pass (lately.html:1227-1236, cited by the seat as 1195-1204 -- the only inaccuracy in the finding, and it is a line-number slip, not a factual one) sets --h to 46, --f to 0.4, redistributes --x, and strips .part and .zero: it neutralises every magnitude that carries GEOMETRY and touches no text node. The gate confirmation is exact: interaction-check.mjs:1441-1446 is six ok() calls reading barHeights, meterFills, .part count, .zero count, dot --x against the fixture, and record-tag visibility -- not one reads text, and grep for 'user-select' or 'selection' across interaction-check.mjs returns nothing, so the gate is structurally blind to this door and stays green. This is not a re-raise of skeleton-draws-the-data-it-says-it-is-still-reading (r2): that closed the painted magnitudes, this is the live text underneath them, and the seat says so. The consequence holds too, and I verified the sharpest part of it: at ?state=partial the overdue card resolves to NOT AVAILABLE with 'Timeline did not answer this reading, so nothing here knows a due date', while the loading selection hands over '2 past the day they were due' in that same slot -- a figure the product may never publish, displayed at full value in the exact box it would occupy, which is the fabricated-figure class the honest-degradation contract exists to forbid, reached from the side. Severity holds at defect and the seat calibrated it honestly rather than reaching for misleading: nothing is put in front of a passive reader, the leak requires a deliberate keystroke, and the state's spoken line ('Loading this reading.') and its aria-hidden wrap are both correct. The proposed fix is right and its numbers are right. I applied '.sk-wrap{-webkit-user-select:none;user-select:none}' and re-drove at 390/768/1280/1440: Ctrl+A then returns the header, the tab strip, the reading rule, 'Loading this reading.' and the three refusals and nothing else -- exactly what the seat promised -- and the bounding boxes of all 49 skeleton elements plus a full-page screenshot are byte-identical before and after at every width, so nothing moves. The seat's rejection of U+2007 is also correct reasoning and worth keeping in the record. The rule is scoped to .sk-wrap, which exists only in the loading state, so no other state and no live reading loses selectability.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as written -- add '-webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none;' to the .sk-wrap rule at lately.html:486, beside the pointer-events: none already there for the same reason, with the comment saying why (a state that says it has not read the numbers may not hand them over). Two additions. (1) The brief prices an assertion that cannot fail above the defect that exposes it, and this finding exposes six of them: the block at interaction-check.mjs:1441-1446 cannot fail on a text leak because it reads only custom properties, class names and visibility. Add a seventh assertion in that same block that reads TEXT, not geometry: select the document (page.keyboard.press('ControlOrMeta+a')) at ?state=loading and assert String(window.getSelection()) contains none of the fixture's own magnitudes -- drive them from window.LATELY_FIXTURE rather than typing '31' and '41', so the assertion cannot go vacuous when the fixture changes. Assert the same of the selection's length against the known non-skeleton copy, so a future skeleton that adds a leaf is caught too. (2) Record, on the port packet rather than as a fix, that find-in-page is not closed by user-select: Blink's text-match markers repaint matched text in the search foreground colour, so Ctrl+F for a number still reveals it in the skeleton. I did not measure that (it is browser chrome, not page), and it is the acceptable residue: a reader who types '31' already holds the number, so nothing is handed to them. Selection and copy are the doors that hand over a reading unasked, and this closes both.
